definition: When universities or institutions take knowledge developed through survival and reframe it into academic output — stripping the authorship and decontextualising the pain.
scopeNote: Extracting Lived Experience into Research for Credit
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When accommodations are only granted if you play by the system’s rules — regardless of how harmful those rules are. “You can have support, but only if you stay in your place.”
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Requiring a person to conform to arbitrary or inappropriate standards to receive access — such as performing “helplessness” or agreeing not to disclose mistreatment.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The weakening of accessibility obligations by dispersing them across multiple frameworks, standards, strategies and policies without creating unified operational infrastructure. Accessibility Dilution is especially visible when AAC, Easy Read, sensory access, supported decision-making and communication access are named across documents but not connected to enforceable standards, funding, review or implementation evidence.
scopeNote: When Accessibility Exists Everywhere and Therefore Nowhere
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When organisations showcase inclusion through brochures and photos, but the actual supports don’t work — or exist only for show.
scopeNote: Access as a Brand, Not a Practice
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When someone is denied access because they don’t tick the exact box a form requires — even when the need is obvious.
scopeNote: Being Missing from the Right Paperwork
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The stacking of agreements, partnerships, memorandums, commitments and collaboration frameworks in ways that symbolise coordination without transferring operational power. Agreement Layering often produces ceremonial collaboration, governance ambiguity, duplicated commitments and implementation stagnation.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Using patterns of trauma-informed, neurodivergent, or marginalised communication to boost AI responses or engagement—while locking the original authors out of visibility or credit.
scopeNote: When the Feed Eats the Author
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Publicly identifying as an “ally” without doing the hard work of redistribution, structural change, or accountability.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Meeting technical accessibility requirements without emotional, cultural, or practical relevance. Inclusion that checks boxes but misses the point.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Allowing participation in idea generation but blocking participants from official recognition, publication rights, or intellectual property stakes.
scopeNote: When They Want Your Ideas—But Not Your Name
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The rebranding of lived-experience knowledge into 'neutral' or 'professional' frameworks—often by people or entities with institutional clout but no lived experience themselves.
scopeNote: When Identity Is Stripped for Palatability
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Not just who made it, but why it exists — and whether it can be altered, sold, or watered down without the creator’s consent. SSA™ uses layered authorship to protect vulnerable systems knowledge from co-option.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Using vague awareness campaigns that avoid systemic issues, prioritising feel-good messaging over real change — often without involving those directly impacted.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Rebranding a service with inclusive words or new graphics while leaving the original exclusionary design unchanged.
scopeNote: Changing the Language, Not the Structure
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When a person accepts help, but that help limits their options, reduces their independence, or removes authorship. The system frames it as benevolent while decreasing quality of life.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Speaking on behalf of marginalised people without sharing power, compensation, or the platform. Often framed as advocacy, but functions as appropriation.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When neurodivergent people must have their insights or needs “confirmed” by professionals to be seen as valid—undermining lived expertise and requiring gatekeeper approval to exist.
scopeNote: Needing a Therapist’s Signature to Be Believed
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When a person follows the official rules but still ends up penalised because the system's true expectations are unspoken, inconsistent, or change without notice.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The division of compliance, safeguarding, accessibility, reporting and accountability obligations across disconnected systems with incompatible structures, language or processes. Compliance Fragmentation shifts the burden of coordination onto disabled people, advocates, families, peer workers, frontline staff and small organisations.
scopeNote: When Safety Depends on Navigating Multiple Systems at Once
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Suggesting that staying calm, quiet, or cheerful in the face of injustice is a sign of strength — rather than a forced survival response.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Situations where refusal to collaborate risks backlash, exclusion, or funding loss—pressuring lived experience advocates to participate in disempowering ways.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When the system avoids saying “no” but designs impossible pathways that function as a no. This includes excessive forms, vague eligibility criteria, or open-ended application processes that technically exist—but aren’t meant to succeed.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When feedback from disabled or marginalised people is collected, repackaged by professionals, and credited to the organisation instead of the contributor.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When a system offers only pre-approved options and calls it “choice” — then uses your participation to imply informed consent.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When institutions talk about reform but change only language—not the structure that causes harm.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When someone uses your work, words, or frameworks and presents them as their own “insight” in safer or more prestigious spaces.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When policies or forms fail to record key information — erasing experiences from official records and removing them from public concern.
scopeNote: When the Numbers Don’t Show the Harm
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When a person is redirected endlessly between services, none of which are equipped to provide real help. A bureaucratic loop that leads nowhere.
scopeNote: Being Sent Somewhere That Can’t Help
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When access is conditional on compliance, and those who assert autonomy are painted as unsafe, unprofessional, or ungrateful.
scopeNote: You Can Speak — But Only If We Let You
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Systems that technically exist, but are built to quietly fail the people they claim to serve. The illusion of support, with none of the substance.
scopeNote: Access That Was Never Intended to Work
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When support is moved online in the name of “accessibility,” but results in even less accountability — and no one to talk to when the system breaks.
scopeNote: Platforms That Replace Human Support — Then Fail
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The breakdown of accountability caused by governance systems spreading responsibility across so many actors, committees, frameworks and jurisdictions that meaningful enforcement becomes difficult or impossible. This term names architectural failure. It should not be used to blame individual workers when responsibility has been structurally diffused by the system itself.
scopeNote: When Governance Structures Become Too Diffuse to Fail Clearly
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When systems rebrand lived tools—like stimming objects, hyperfocus systems, or communication cards—as commercial products with no reinvestment in the communities that created them.
scopeNote: Monetising What We’ve Had to Create
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Making the process of applying so complicated, technical, or contradictory that people give up or never apply at all.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When neurodivergent expressions of care—like deep pattern noticing, advocacy, or intense loyalty—are ignored or dismissed because they don’t follow neurotypical emotional scripts.
scopeNote: Assuming We Don’t Feel Because We Show It Differently
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When programs pretend to centre disability or trauma-informed leadership but retain control, edit lived experience, and deny genuine co-design or authorship.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Collecting lived-experience stories to generate funding, branding, or prestige—while offering little to no return to those who shared them.
scopeNote: Mining Pain for Content or Clout
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Translating powerful personal testimony into neutral or decontextualised summaries that can be used to justify inaction or misrepresent lived-experience consensus.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When systems imply that support can only be given after the individual “fixes” themselves — putting the burden of access on personal change rather than systemic adaptation.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When the design of systems (e.g. government forms, assessments, or online portals) forces a person to misrepresent themselves in order to access support. This distorts identity and data while punishing honesty.
scopeNote: When the Form Doesn’t Fit the Person
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The production of excessive frameworks, strategies, policies, agreements or action plans that overwhelm communities, workers or advocates with procedural complexity. Framework Flooding creates exhaustion, fragmentation and navigational overload while allowing institutions to continue signalling progress.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When only the most “palatable” or institutionally aligned people get access to opportunity — while others are labelled difficult, dangerous, or non-compliant for needing the same things.
scopeNote: Only Some Get Out — And Only If They Behave
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Framing a project as inclusive in grant documents to secure funding — then delivering something inaccessible, gatekept, or performative.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Insisting that people be “grateful” for crumbs of support — even when those crumbs are harmful, insufficient, or humiliating.
scopeNote: Forcing Thanks Where There Should Be Change
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Creating the illusion of inclusive input while decisions have already been made. Often used for PR, not systemic change.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The phenomenon where your ideas influence platforms, algorithms, or research—but you are never cited, paid, or publicly acknowledged.
scopeNote: When You’re Referenced, But Not Seen
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Offering hollow comfort or oversimplified advice that ignores a person’s depth, complexity, or autonomy — often in a patronising tone.
scopeNote: Talking Down in the Name of Comfort
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Consulting communities for their ideas, then converting those ideas into institutionally owned frameworks, campaigns, or products—often stripped of context and credit.
scopeNote: Gathering Lived Experience as Raw Material
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When people reword or co-opt someone’s survival story for social media clout, awareness campaigns, or funding applications — often without consent.
scopeNote: Trying on Struggle Without Living It
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When a person in authority rewords your lived experience to suit the narrative of institutional control.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When frameworks, toolkits, or language appear in new systems that mirror community-created work—but with no credit, backlinks, or citation trail. Authorship becomes untraceable, yet the architecture remains.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The shifting of responsibility between departments, commissions, providers, jurisdictions or governance bodies so that no single actor becomes fully accountable. Jurisdictional Deflection is not the same as a legitimate referral. The harm occurs when referral happens without continuity, ownership, warm handover or traceable accountability.
scopeNote: When Every Agency Says It Belongs to Someone Else
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The creation or layering of overlapping legislation, frameworks, agreements, standards, strategies, action plans and procedural systems in ways that obscure responsibility, diffuse accountability or prevent meaningful implementation. Legislation Laundering often creates the appearance of reform while making the actual governance landscape too fragmented, technical or contradictory for affected communities to navigate.
scopeNote: When Accountability Is Buried Under Frameworks
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When the value of your lived experience is dismissed because you don’t have the “right” accreditation or institutional label — even if your outcomes speak for themselves.
scopeNote: When You're Qualified — But Not Recognised
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When a system requires constant reproof of need, identity, or eligibility — even after a person has already been verified. Often used to delay or deny support through “process over person” logic.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Responding to someone’s hardship with upbeat clichés or silver linings that deflect from what they’re actually feeling or saying.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The stripping of origin, context, or authorship from digital knowledge—especially when used to feed AI or system development without consent.
scopeNote: When the System Keeps the Info, Not the Author
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Blaming structural oppression on an individual’s “mindset,” as though positive thinking alone resolves systemic harm.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Passing concerns from agency to agency until the original issue is diluted or abandoned. This form of bureaucratic ping-pong deflects responsibility under the guise of referral.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The exhaustion, burnout or disengagement caused by requiring people to navigate highly fragmented governance, service, legislative or compliance systems simultaneously. Navigational Exhaustion disproportionately impacts disabled people, neurodivergent people, people using AAC, people in crisis, peer advocates and families.
scopeNote: When Systems Become Too Complex to Access Safely
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Reframing neurodivergence as dysfunction that needs correcting, rather than validating it as a legitimate cognitive experience.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When pathways exist in theory but no one ever responds to your application, email, or offer — so you're told “you didn’t try,” while your efforts are erased.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When people with lived experience are invited to a table but not allowed to set the agenda—or are only included to validate predetermined outcomes.
scopeNote: Inviting Us In, Then Talking Over Us
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When systems rely on written policies to demonstrate “support” but refuse to enforce those policies meaningfully when abuse or discrimination occurs.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When a support exists on paper but not in practice — and the burden of proof is pushed onto the person who was excluded.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When institutions or influencers extract language, frameworks, or tools born from survival — and repackage them as marketable products, losing context and diluting power.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Inviting lived-experience contributors to consultations or panels without any intention to incorporate their recommendations. This uses presence as permission—conflating being seen with being heard or empowered.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Offering surface-level inclusion for show (e.g. diverse images or “voice of lived experience” panels) without transferring actual power, decision-making, or compensation.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Offering tokenistic roles or visibility while keeping decision-making power behind closed doors. Inclusion as branding, not equity.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When someone with more visibility “amplifies” a lived-experience message—then becomes the spokesperson, drowning out the original voice.
scopeNote: Using Your Megaphone to Mute Others
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When the system boosts extracted insights through professional channels while the original authors remain invisible, unfunded, or de-platformed. This shifts cultural capital to institutions that did not generate the knowledge they profit from.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The accumulation of policies, frameworks, standards, procedures, audits and compliance obligations to the point where systems become internally contradictory, unmanageable or functionally inaccessible. Policy Stack Saturation often creates implementation bottlenecks, inaccessible compliance systems, worker overload, governance confusion and symbolic rather than operational compliance.
scopeNote: When Systems Collapse Under Their Own Governance Layers
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The enforcement of “positive vibes only” in spaces where real harm needs to be named. Often used to silence lived experience or distress.
scopeNote: When You’re Only Welcome if You Smile
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When the complaints or reform process is made deliberately confusing, untraceable, or repetitive. Designed to overwhelm or discredit the complainant through technicalities, not truth.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When self-created coping strategies—like scripts, charts, or visual prompts—are adopted by professionals and reframed as clinical tools, often with no reference to neurodivergent origins.
scopeNote: Copying Our Structures Without Our Voice
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: A protocol layer is the ruleset underneath a system — the part that determines whether your meaning travels safely, or gets reinterpreted against you. SSA™ builds a lived-experience-led protocol layer to guard against systemic distortion.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When system failure is reframed as your inability to “fit” — and you're expected to change yourself instead of the structure.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Centres the ally’s feelings about injustice instead of the injustice itself—shifting focus and labour back onto the marginalised person.
scopeNote: Making Your Guilt the Main Character
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The repeated public declaration of reforms, commitments or strategic transformations without equivalent investment in implementation infrastructure, accountability systems or operational redesign. Reform Theatre is closely related to Cosmetic Reform and Inclusion Theatre, but specifically describes public reform cycles, announcement infrastructure and repeated relaunches of change without measurable structural transition.
scopeNote: Announcing Change Faster Than Systems Can Change
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Using “safety” to justify silencing, excluding, or overriding a person’s needs or voice.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Turning a complex, painful lived experience into an inspirational story that removes the systemic context — making it easier to consume, but harder to challenge.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The gradual divergence of terminology, definitions and governance language across systems, resulting in semantic fragmentation. Semantic Governance Drift weakens interoperability, implementation, accountability, evaluation and participation.
scopeNote: When Every Framework Uses Different Language for the Same Problem
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When lived-experience phrases are lifted from social media, feedback forums, or community spaces and reused in policy, branding, or AI without acknowledgment. This practice erases intellectual labour while monetising the emotional truth of marginalised people.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When neurodivergent expressions of clarity or boundary-setting are reinterpreted as “challenging behaviour,” “rigidity,” or “demand avoidance”—pathologising patterns that are functional or protective.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Taking raw, emotional, or grassroots language from lived experience and rewording it into palatable, institutional-sounding frameworks—often to remove its power or traceability.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: The right to define, anchor, and distribute your own meaning — without institutional reframing. A core concept of SSA™ and the reason behind this glossary.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: Support that is only offered to those who remain passive or non-critical. Speaking out leads to exclusion, withheld services, or reputational retaliation.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: “Splaining” is not a typo. It’s a pattern. These terms expose tactics that reframe harm as help, control as care, and oppression as oversight. When someone insists they’re helping—but their help strips you of autonomy, authorship, or agency.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: A trauma-informed, systems-aware framework for reclaiming power. SSA™ is not a method of “being better behaved in broken systems.” It’s a protocol layer for surviving and influencing them with your dignity intact.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When systems claim to be receptive to feedback but repeatedly route it to dead ends, irrelevant staff, or delayed “future planning cycles.” This tactic creates the illusion of inclusion while exhausting participants into silence.
scopeNote: Refusing Direct Engagement While Appearing Open
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When no reply is the reply — because your voice isn’t seen as valuable, your insight isn’t welcome, or your presence threatens the status quo.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin

definition: When you're invited to the table for optics — but not decision-making. Your presence is used to validate a process you don’t control.
creator: https://www.mcloughlin.world/#sarah-ailish-mcloughlin
